## V-010 — CREDIT-ETF (IDEA-010) — *required by the Cycle-32 top-three rule* — **NEVER TO BE EXECUTED — the candidate was parked (P-014) in Cycle 78** — specification only, never executed here

**Status: never to be executed — the candidate was parked (P-014) in Cycle 78.** G-34 was executed as a
bounded literature operation in Cycle 77 and its **pre-registered kill condition fired**: no published
work decomposes a corporate-bond ETF's ETF–NAV discount into a **transient** and a **mechanical**
component, and no published work identifies a **published, decision-time** state that discriminates
between the two in the corporate-bond ETF universe without the ETF→AP mapping that G-29/G-30 established
is unavailable. The candidate's residual is therefore **unmeasurable as specified**, and per the Cycle-76
decision rule it was **re-classified (downgraded or parked), not re-specified** — the register chose
**park** (see `rejected_and_parked.md`, **P-014**). Two facts bear directly on this specification's
executability and are unchanged by the parking: **G-29** returned **0 corporate-bond ETFs with a published
AP set** (the naming practice is confined to the crypto and commodity-trust class, S-239), and **G-30**
is **exhausted** across all four routes outside the statutory prospectus — so the state-construction step
of this specification **cannot be performed** in the candidate's universe, and no published crowding proxy
may be substituted for the missing mapping. **This specification is retained for the record only and must
not be executed.** It is not a candidate specification any more, and **no re-specification may be written
around a weaker state while the candidate is parked**. The register's rule that "a null obtained under one
convention is not a kill" and its "untested, not dead" verdict are **not** available here: this
specification is blocked by the **absence of an executable state**, not by a missing test.

**Why this specification exists.** IDEA-010 entered the top three for the first time in Cycle 32 (68.0,
rank 3), and **G-16 — the precondition that blocked every specification for this candidate since
Cycle 6 — is now closed in the candidate's favour**. The validation is therefore no longer required
against the register's original target (disclosed dealer funding value adjustments), which Cycle 32
showed to be unusable: a dealer's FVA is an OTC-derivatives-specific, annual/quarterly and frequently
immaterial disclosure, and no continuous public FVA series exists (S-155). Independent published work
has performed the validation the register wanted, on a better target and on exactly the link the
candidate claims: Raddatz (S-194) constructs the authorized-participant set for each US corporate-bond
ETF from SEC regulatory filings, measures **APs' regulatory capital ratios**, and shows that the ratio
— not equity/assets, cash/assets, total assets or activity concentration — governs ETF arbitrage
intensity and ETF premia, materially so during the March 2020 dash-for-cash. The mechanism is published
(S-195), and three published rival explanations now stand against the candidate's interpretation
(S-196 fractional baskets, S-197 funding segmentation, S-199 client liquidity discounts).
**What remains open is registered as gap G-23** (cadence, and signedness of the state). This document
is a *specification*: no data were acquired, no test was run, and no result is reported or implied.

**Cycle 34 amendment (G-23 — cadence and signedness).**
- **Cadence (binding limitation):** AP regulatory capital ratios are taken from SEC filings (Form 10-K/10-Q) for bank holding companies and broker-dealers, with a filing lag (typically 40-45 days after quarter end). The state updates **only on filing dates** and must be held constant until the next filing. For a 1-10 session holding horizon as specified, the state is **quarterly at best** and is stale relative to the trading horizon — this is a material feasibility constraint. The validator must report the fraction of trading days covered by a single state reading and explicitly acknowledge staleness. If the 1-10 session rule proves infeasible due to cadence, the horizon must be extended or the candidate reconsidered for parking.
- **Signedness (mandatory test):** The state must be tested for signedness against the three published rivals: S-196 (fractional baskets), S-197 (funding segmentation), S-199 (client liquidity discounts). The joint condition (weak AP capital ratios AND net redemption flow) remains required; ablations must include (a) state alone, (b) flow alone, (c) joint, and (d) each rival explanation controlled for separately. The candidate is a trade specification and cost-floor test on a published relation, not a discovery of the relation.

**Cycle 35 amendment (G-23 — closed in the candidate's favour; the cadence is resolved by re-anchoring the
identification, and the signedness becomes a pre-registered, killable first test).**
- **Cadence — resolved; the horizon is preserved; the candidate is not parked.** The state is refreshed
  only when an AP files: Form 10-Q within **40 days** of quarter end for large accelerated and
  accelerated filers and **45 days** for all other registrants, annual reports at 60/75/90 days by filer
  status (S-225), and FR Y-9C at 40 calendar days after the March/June/September as-of dates and 45 after
  December (S-226). That is at best quarterly and lagged. The resolution is that **the claim never
  required the state to change inside the holding window**: it requires the *level* of the AP set's
  capital ratio to govern the *size* of the flow-induced discount widening and its reversion, and a
  state held constant between filings is fully usable for a claim of that form — the published relation
  itself (S-194) identifies the state at filing frequency. Two consequences are binding:
  1. **The primary identification is cross-sectional.** Weak-capital ETFs versus strong-capital ETFs
     on redemption days, with the state read as of the last filing date and held constant between
     filings. The within-ETF time-series reading — a state *change* producing a discount *change* — is
     demoted to a **low-power ablation** and must be reported as such, with its own effective-sample
     count.
  2. **The effective sample must be reported, and "untested" remains a permitted verdict.** The
     informative units are (ETF, filing-date) state observations and the redemption days inside them.
     The validator must report: the number of ETFs whose AP set is reconstructable; the number of
     filing-date state observations; the number of those in which the state is bottom-tercile; and the
     number of redemption days inside bottom-tercile observations. If those counts are too small for
     inference, the validator reports the candidate as **untested — not dead** — and must not upgrade a
     small-sample null into a kill.
- **No horizon extension.** The 1–10 session exit continues to govern the *reversion of the flow-induced
  widening*; the refresh cadence of the state does not enter the exit. This amendment does not
  authorise a horizon extension, and the candidate is not parked on cadence grounds.
- **Signedness — now the first pre-registered, killable test.** The published relation (S-194) is
  signed and monotone in the capital state (a 0.69pp versus 0.39pp decline in arbitrage intensity for
  bottom- versus top-quartile capital ratios), so the state is signed in the mechanism's direction and
  not merely a moderator. The signed prediction the validator must register **first** is: *on redemption
  days, weak-capital ETFs' discounts widen more than strong-capital ETFs' discounts*, measured as the
  change in the ETF–NAV discount from the pre-redemption baseline with ETF fixed effects absorbing the
  level. The three mandatory rival controls are unchanged but are now specified as **controls on the
  interaction**, not on the level:
  1. *Fractional baskets* (S-196) — basket composition must be shown not to explain the *level* of the
     discount; the test is run on the discount's *change*.
  2. *Funding segmentation* (S-197) — controlled for with public funding-state variables, so that an AP
     funding shock is separated from an AP capital constraint.
  3. *Client liquidity discounts* (S-199) — the bond-side cheapening must be shown to be specific to the
     ETF's own AP set and redemption days, rather than a dealer-relationship discount visible in the
     bond market broadly.
  The monthly published dispersion proxy (S-200) remains a robustness check with its monthly frequency
  acknowledged; aggregate dealer financial-soundness averages remain a documented inferiority (S-200),
  not an alternative.
- **Hard-stop flag added.** The candidate must not be presented as a discovery of the state-to-premium
  relation (published: S-194, S-195), and must not be presented as evidence that a *session-refreshed*
  capital state is tradeable: the state is a **slow filter**, and the rule is a cross-sectional
  contrast.
- **Open residual — G-27.** The per-AP filing frequency and the cross-regime comparability of the
  capital ratio (broker-dealer versus bank holding company versus asset manager) and the

**Cycle 37 amendment (G-27 — closed in the candidate's favour on state availability; the state-

### Frozen hypothesis
When corporate-bond ETF redemptions meet an authorized-participant set whose regulatory capital ratios
are weak, the APs cannot absorb the delivered bonds onto their balance sheets at the speed the flow
requires; the ETF therefore trades at a wider discount to its NAV, and the underlying bonds cheapen
relative to the ETF. A participant who supplies the liquidity the AP cannot — long the discounted ETF
against the underlying basket — earns the concession when the AP set's capacity recovers and the discount
narrows. The *joint* conditioning (weak AP capital ratios **and** net redemption flow) is the claim;
neither leg alone is.

### Frozen conceptual rules
- **State (the AP-set regulatory capital ratio), constructed exactly as in S-194 and fixed ex ante.**
  For each ETF, the AP set is identified from the sponsor's public disclosures; for each AP, the
  regulatory capital ratio is taken from its SEC filings (Form 10-K/10-Q capital disclosures, and the
  equivalent for bank holding companies) at the most recent filing date; the ETF-level state is a
  pre-registered aggregate of that set (e.g. a cap-weighted median of the set's ratios, or the set's
  minimum — the validator must pre-register one aggregation and report the others as ablations).
  The state enters the rule **only from the filing date forward**; no filing is used before its public
  date.
- **Flow leg: net creations/redemptions, from the sponsor's published daily shares outstanding.** The
  signal is the change in shares outstanding over a pre-registered window, and its sign is defined
  ex ante (a decrease in shares outstanding = net redemption = the adverse flow). No other flow
  measure is allowed in the trigger.
- **Trigger: the joint condition.** The trade is opened only when the AP-set capital ratio is in the
  bottom tercile of its own trailing history *as of the last filing date* **and** the flow leg is
  adverse (net redemptions). The tercile is computed on the training window only and then frozen.
- **Leg 1 (the long leg): long the ETF.** Sized at a pre-registered fraction of the discount, or at a
  pre-registered fixed notional; the sizing rule must be fixed on the training window.
- **Leg 2 (the short leg): the underlying basket.** The ETF's published holdings (or its published
  creation-basket composition) define the basket; the short must be implemented in the way the
  validator pre-registers, and the validator must report the **shortability of the basket** as a first
  class result, because a basket that cannot be borrowed is a *cost* result and not a *kill* of the
  candidate — the register distinguishes the two.
- **Exit: pre-scheduled, not state-dependent.** The position is exited at a pre-registered horizon of
  1 to 10 sessions after entry (fixed at the training window, or a fixed grid reported separately),
  because the candidate's claim is a *reversion within 1–10 sessions*. No discretionary exit.
- **No look-ahead.** The ETF–NAV discount is *measured* at and after entry, never used as an input to
  the trigger. The discount may be used for sizing only if the sizing rule is frozen in advance.

### Ambiguities the validator must resolve and record
1. The ETF universe and its AP set per ETF, with the disclosure used for each mapping, and the
   treatment of ETFs whose AP set cannot be reconstructed (they must be dropped and the drop reported,
   not silently imputed).
2. The regulatory-capital-ratio definition used per AP type (broker-dealer, bank holding company,
   asset manager) and how non-comparable capital regimes are handled.
3. Whether the state is a level, a change, or a percentile of its own history, and how the tercile is
   set without peeking.
4. The NAV used for the discount (official end-of-day NAV, intraday indicative value, or a
   reconstructed basket mark) and the resulting measurement error, including stale-bond pricing inside
   the NAV.
5. The short-leg implementation and its borrow cost, including the possibility that the basket cannot
   be shorted.
6. The treatment of corporate-action and index-rebalance days inside the holding window.

### Target universe, time frame, sampling frequency
- Universe: US-listed corporate-bond ETFs (investment-grade and high-yield) whose AP set can be
  reconstructed from public filings, and their published underlying baskets.
- Time frame: the full history for which the ETF's AP set, the APs' filings and daily shares
  outstanding are all available — with the **March 2020 dash-for-cash window mandatory** in the
  sample, because that is the episode in which the state was published to bind (S-194), and with a
  pre- vs post-2020 split reported, because the RFS-style regulatory regimes and the ETF market have
  both changed.
- Sampling frequency: the **state is quarterly** (it changes only when an AP files); the **flow leg is
  daily**; the **position is daily**. This is a real constraint and the validator must state, in the
  results, how much of the sample is covered by a single filing.

### Data fields required
ETF daily market price, official NAV and intraday indicative value; daily shares outstanding and the
published creation/redemption basket composition; the ETF's holdings file; AP identifiers and their SEC
filings; TRACE bond prices and volumes for the basket and for the financing of the short leg; borrow
availability and cost for the short leg; and ETF bid-ask spreads.

### Timing, execution and survivorship
- AP capital ratios enter only on their filing dates; the state is then held constant until the next
  filing, which must be modelled explicitly (no retrospective revision).
- ETF survivorship: an ETF that merges, closes or changes its index must be handled explicitly, and
  the effect of dropping the pre-merger history must be reported.
- AP-set survivorship: an AP that leaves the AP set must be handled, and the rule for a set that
  changes between filings must be pre-registered.
- Parameter and threshold choices are made on the training window only; the holdout opens once.

### Cost and execution assumptions the validator must justify independently
ETF bid-ask spreads and market impact on the long leg; the cost and feasibility of shorting the
basket, including the financing and recall risk of a corporate-bond short; the ETF's own creation and
redemption mechanics as an alternative implementation of leg 2 (and their costs); financing on the long
leg; and the effect of the position size relative to the ETF's daily volume and to the basket's TRACE
depth. The validator must state whether the trade survives these assumptions at the pre-specified size,
and must report the **cost floor** explicitly, because a gross discount below the round-trip cost is a
kill condition in the candidate's own terms.

### Pre-specified primary outcome and guardrails
- **Primary:** the average net return of the **joint-conditioned** trade, and its difference against
  the **unconditioned** ETF-versus-basket basis trade over the same dates, on a pre-specified
  risk-adjusted measure. The joint conditioning is the claim; the unconditional basis trade is the
  baseline that the trade must beat.
- **Mandatory ablations that are part of the primary result (not extras):** (a) the state leg alone;
  (b) the flow leg alone; (c) the joint condition. If the joint condition does not add to the single
  legs, the candidate is dead, and the validator must say so rather than reporting only the best leg.
- **Rival-exclusion results, mandatory:** (i) *fractional baskets* (S-196) — does the discount persist
  after controlling for the ETF's basket composition; (ii) *funding segmentation* (S-197) — is the
  discount explained by a funding-segregation shock rather than by AP capacity; (iii) *client liquidity
  discounts* (S-199) — is the bond-side cheapening a dealer relationship-discount phenomenon rather
  than an ETF-arbiter phenomenon; and (iv) the **monthly-frequency** published dispersion proxy
  (S-200) as a robustness check on the state.
- Guardrails: maximum drawdown, worst single event, worst calendar window, worst single-day loss,
  loss attributable to the worst three events as a share of cumulative profit, turnover and round-trip
  cost, borrow recall events, and the gross-versus-net decomposition of every reported return.

### Stress cases, regime slices, ablations
- Regime slices: the March 2020 dash-for-cash window; other credit-stress episodes; high vs low
  aggregate ETF redemption flow; periods of wide vs narrow ETF spreads; pre- vs post-2020.
- Ablations: (a) the state replaced by the published interdealer dispersion proxy (S-200), acknowledging
  its monthly frequency; (b) the state replaced by an aggregate dealer financial-weakness proxy, which
  S-200 documents to be inferior — reported to show the difference, not as a candidate; (c) the flow leg
  replaced by a market-wide ETF-flow proxy to separate ETF-specific from market-wide redemption; and
  (d) an explicit count of every (state definition × aggregation × exit rule × universe) combination
  examined, with every rule change logged with a date and a reason.

### Pass / fail / uncertain
- **Pass:** the joint-conditioned trade beats the unconditional basis trade on the pre-specified
  risk-adjusted measure after justified costs; the discount widens in the conditioned state relative to
  its own history; the discount mean-reverts within the pre-registered horizon; and the result survives
  the three mandatory rival-exclusion controls and the monthly-proxy robustness check.
- **Fail:** no joint conditioning (the single legs do all the work); no mean-reversion inside the
  horizon; the gross discount below the round-trip cost in every ETF; or the effect explained by
  fractional baskets, funding segmentation or client liquidity discounts.
- **Uncertain:** the AP set cannot be reconstructed for enough of the sample, or the sample contains
  too few quarters with a bottom-tercile state for inference — report the descriptive behaviour and
  state that the candidate is untested rather than concluding.

### Kill criteria and follow-up justification
Kill if the joint conditioning adds nothing to the single legs after costs, or if the round-trip cost
exceeds the gross discount in every selected ETF, or if the rival-exclusion controls absorb the
effect. Justify follow-up research if the effect survives costs but is concentrated in one episode
(2020) or in one ETF type — that points to a capacity-and-selection problem, and would motivate a
narrower, more specialised candidate rather than a general edge.

### Register notes carried into execution
- The state is **public in principle and lagged**: quarterly filings, with a filing lag (S-225,
  S-226). **G-23 is now closed in the candidate's favour** (Cycle 35): the cadence is handled by
  re-anchoring the identification to a cross-sectional contrast and by demoting the time-series
  reading to a low-power ablation, so the 1–10 session horizon is preserved and the candidate is not
  parked. The validator must still report the effective-sample counts — the number of (ETF,
  filing-date) state observations, the number in a bottom-tercile state, and the number of redemption
  days inside them — and **"untested" remains a permitted verdict** where those counts are too small
  for inference. The per-AP frequency and cross-regime comparability of the capital ratio are the
  open residual **G-27**.
- The register's rule that "no specification is to be written until G-16 is closed" is now satisfied;
  **G-16 is closed in the candidate's favour** and **V-010 is executable as specified**, subject to the
  validator's own data and implementation checks.
- The candidate is **not** a discovery of the state-to-premium relation: that relation is published
  (S-194, S-195). What is untested is the **trade specification and the cost floor**, and the
  validator's report must be framed accordingly.
- The signed prediction is now the candidate's **first pre-registered, killable test** (Cycle-35
  amendment): on redemption days, weak-capital ETFs' discounts widen more than strong-capital ETFs'
  discounts, with the three rival controls (S-196, S-197, S-199) applied to the *interaction* rather
  than to the level, and the monthly dispersion proxy (S-200) as a robustness check.

- **Cycle-40 amendment (G-29 executed; the state-construction step is not executable on the candidate's
  universe from public filings).** G-29 was executed as a *calibrated document-level search*: the
  register's trade-press lead was verified from the primary document (S-239 — the iShares Bitcoin Trust
  ETF Form 424B3 prospectuses name their authorised participants verbatim, five APs in January 2024 (nine by April, twelve by August 2024)
  and twelve cash plus four in-kind as of 31 July 2025), which supplied a detector known to work. Run
  across every prospectus form type, that detector returns **five documents in four filers — every one a
  crypto or commodity trust — and no corporate-bond ETF**; the phrase-first route over 591 bond-worded
  filings and the name-first route over bond-worded filings containing any of thirty-one AP firm names
  return the same answer, and two sponsor product pages (iShares AGG, Vanguard BND) name no AP.
  **Coverage count: 0 corporate-bond ETFs with a published AP set; 0 (ETF, AP) cells; 0 (ETF, AP,
  episode) cells.** Consequences for a validator, in order of importance:
  1. **The state-construction step of this specification cannot currently be performed for a
     corporate-bond ETF.** The capital state itself is abundant (2,419+ broker-dealer filers, S-231);
     what does not exist publicly is the **ETF → AP mapping**. A validator must therefore **not**
     substitute a published crowding proxy (S-026's Days-ADV, S-157's comomentum, S-222's crowding
     factor) for the mapping: those measure all 13F institutions, i.e. directional positioning, and the
     candidate's claim is about arbitrage capital. Such a substitution converts the candidate into a
     known baseline and is prohibited by the register's rule.
  2. **If** a validator can obtain an AP mapping for a corporate-bond ETF from a source outside the
     statutory prospectus (this is what **G-30** asks for — a sponsor-published participant list, an
     exchange or regulatory disclosure requirement, or a non-US issuer's prospectus), then the
     specification becomes executable and the mapping route must be **documented in the report**, with
     the document, its date and its granularity.
  3. **The effective-sample report must use the Cycle-40 denominators**, which are the first worked
     (ETF, AP, episode) counts in the register: on the one published AP set in the project (the crypto
     class), **13 distinct named AP firms, 13 of 13 with a public Form X-17A-5 filing, 285 (AP,
     filing-date) cells**, and **none** of the thirteen files a Form 10-Q or 10-K, so Form X-17A-5 is
     the only public capital route for the entire set.
  4. **The cadence premise is corrected.** The private-AP capital state is **annual** — fiscal year-end,
     filed February–March — and therefore **9–14 months stale** at any decision date; the Cycle-37
     statement that some private filers report quarterly rests on a single document that does not
     appear in the phrase corpus at all and must be re-verified from that firm's own filing index before

  5. **Form FR Y-9C is not indexed by EDGAR's full-text search at all** (zero hits for "capital", "net

  6. The verdict remains **"untested"** where the counts are too small, and the candidate's status is

### Cycle-76 note (not an amendment — the specification's executability is unchanged) — the trigger-based re-read
that Cycle 75 handed on was executed, and it adds two mandatory controls and one open question
- **What changed.** Cycle 75 registered **S-331** as a published neighbour touching the candidate's
  flow-impact premise and **handed the re-read on**, because S-331 was index-rendered and the register's rule
  forbids using an index-rendered source as a verification basis. Cycle 76 **line-verified S-331** (the
  author-hosted PDF fetched directly, HTTP 200, 978,520 bytes, 63 pages, text extracted with `pypdf` — the
  Cycle-75 extraction failure was a **tooling gap, not a document defect**) and **executed the re-read**. The
  published result is a **neighbour of the candidate's mechanism, not the candidate's own relation**, so
  **IDEA-010 keeps 68.0 at rank 2 and this specification's content is not re-specified**; but two things are
  added to the specification's *content* for any future execution, and one question is opened.
- **Mandatory control 1 — the intermediary-attenuation account (S-331).** S-331 establishes that "the price
  impact of investor demand depends critically on institutional structure": a flow executed by a specialised
  intermediary with spare capacity has "statistically insignificant and economically negligible price
  impact", while a mutual-fund flow moved prices by 1.64 % per 1 % of shares outstanding with a significant
  subsequent reversal. The candidate's long leg is an ETF creation/redemption flow executed by an authorised
  participant — a specialised intermediary. **If V-010 is ever executed, the validator must pre-register a
  discriminator** that separates the *transient* reading of the ETF–NAV widening (a temporary price-pressure
  dislocation a liquidity supplier can monetise) from the *mechanical* reading (a consequence of intermediated
  creation/redemption pricing and basket composition — S-196). This is a **new mandatory rival-exclusion
  result**, to sit beside the existing three (S-196, S-197, S-199) and to be reported even if it explains the
  effect.
- **Mandatory control 2 — the published competitor conditioner (S-195, now line-verified).** The same paper
  that supplies the candidate's mechanism states that "the sensitivity of ETF arbitrage by APs is declining in
  market volatility, bond market illiquidity and costs of trade" (a one-standard-deviation increase in market
  volatility generates a 10 % decline in AP arbitrage; the decline is larger when the ETF premium is negative).
  Because this conditioner is **available at decision time** in the candidate's universe while the candidate's
  own state is not (G-29, G-30), **any future execution must report the candidate's incremental content
  against this published conditioner**, and must not present the candidate as uniquely state-conditioned.
- **The published sign-reversal mechanism is now part of the risk statement.** S-195 also publishes that "ETF
  arbitrage may go in the opposite direction than what would be implied by the initial relative
  mispricing" — the entity the rule supplies liquidity to may trade *against* the mispricing it is meant to
  correct. The specification's pass/fail language must treat that as a live failure mode and not only as a
  cost or capacity issue.
- **Gap G-34 is opened, and it does not unblock this specification.** G-34 asks whether published work
  decomposes a corporate-bond ETF's ETF–NAV discount into a **transient** and a **mechanical** component and
  identifies a **published, decision-time** state that discriminates between the two **without** the ETF→AP
  mapping. **Kill condition:** if neither the decomposition nor a decision-time discriminating state is
  published, the candidate's residual is **unmeasurable as specified** and the candidate must be
  **re-classified (downgraded or parked), not re-specified** around a weaker state. **V-010 remains
  non-executable** against the corporate-bond ETF universe, because G-29 and G-30 stand; G-30 was **not**
  re-probed in Cycle 76, no statutory filing was re-run and no published crowding proxy was substituted.
- **What is unchanged.** The specification's structure, the 1–10 session horizon, the cross-sectional
  re-anchoring, the effective-sample denominators, the three pre-existing rival controls, the monthly
  dispersion-proxy robustness check (S-200) and the "untested, not dead" verdict are **all unchanged**. This
  is a **note**, not an amendment: no re-specification is written, and no `V-` identifier is consumed.


### Cycle-78 note (not an amendment — this specification is withdrawn from execution) — the G-34 kill condition fired
- **What changed.** The Cycle-77 bounded literature operation executed **G-34** and its **pre-registered kill

- **What the Cycle-78 verification pass adds to the record (no execution authorised).** Four of the

  from the documents themselves: **S-196** (BIS WP 975, fetched directly, 1.7 MB, 54 pages) — "the portfolio
  of bonds that are exchanged for new or existing ETF shares … often represents a small fraction of ETF
  holdings – a fact that we call 'fractional baskets'", "**ETFs with fractional baskets exhibit persistent
  premiums and discounts**, which is related to the slow adjustment of NAV returns to ETF returns", and "an

  **S-198** (OFR WP 22-01) — "while we do not have information on AP-level inventories, we can indirectly

  discounts**"; **S-200** (NBER WP 32998) — "Given the infrequent trading of bonds, calculating interdealer

  soundness **fail** to capture effects from interdealer frictions". **Two of these bear directly on the
  specification's central controls:** the **fractional-basket** account (S-196) is now *documented as
  persistent* rather than transient, and the **SMCCF** episode (S-198) documents the AP-balance-sheet
  channel **in the candidate's own universe** (intraday spillovers within 15 minutes; bonds with more AP
  exposure at lower yield spreads; next-day inflows **at a price premium to NAV**) — so the mechanical
  reading the discriminator was meant to separate is **published in the universe the specification would
  have run in**, which is why the discriminator the Cycle-76 note demanded could not be pre-registered.
- **Re-admission.** If the candidate is ever re-admitted under the **P-014** unblocking condition, this
  specification must be **re-derived from scratch** against the then-current published state, not resumed
  from this text.

## V-012 — RIN-EXISTENCE (IDEA-014) — the candidate's **state-free existence test** — *written under the Cycle-112 narrow amendment to the register's specification rule*

### Authority, scope and what this specification is not

**Authority.** The register's Cycle-6 rule reads: "IDEA-014 … has no specification and must not be given one
until gap **G-15** … is closed". **G-15 is closed on the published-literature side** (Cycle 7) and the
register's own gap table lists it as closed. The dossier's operative formulation — "none may be written until
a pre-deadline, signed state is identified" — was written for the **conditional** version of IDEA-014, which
is **retired with a hard stop** and which is the only version that would require a signed state. **Cycle 112
amends the rule, narrowly and on the record:** a **state-free** specification is now permitted for IDEA-014,
because (i) the candidate's only live claim is the **state-free existence test**, (ii) that test requires
**no signed state by construction** — it asks whether a deadline discontinuity exists in the price data at
all, before any conditional claim is entertained — and (iii) the two agency documents located in Cycle 112
(S-393, S-394) supply the two inputs the Cycle-7 search had recorded as unavailable: a **public,
agency-audited transaction-price dataset** and a **published friction anchor**. **The bar on any
state-conditioned specification for IDEA-014 is re-affirmed in full**: the conditional version stays retired
with its hard stop, G-20 stays closed against the state as specified, and **no specification may be written
for the conditional claim.**

**What this specification is not.** It is **not** a test of the candidate's conditional claim. It does not
assume a sign, does not use the published net obligated position, and does not condition on any
pre-deadline state. It is **not** a trade specification: no position, sizing, horizon or execution rule is
specified, because the candidate's conditional claim is retired. It is a **kill test for the candidate's
existence claim**, and a null result kills that claim.

### Cycle-114 amendment (binding) — the price series' published form is re-specified, the detectability bound is carried into the kill criteria, and the cost anchor's wording is corrected

Cycle 114 executed the Cycle-113 handoff's two remaining re-screen limbs for this candidate and added a third, the
detectability bound. The outcome is a **re-specification of the data requirement** and an **addition to the kill
criteria**; the frozen hypothesis, the statistic, the windows, the controls and the *state-free* scope of this
specification are **unchanged**. **This specification is amended, not re-created.** No `V-` identifier is consumed,
and the standing bar on any state-conditioned specification for IDEA-014 is re-affirmed in full.

1. **The price-series requirement is re-specified, because EPA's public price data are weekly volume-weighted
   averages and not transaction-level prices.** The specification's "**The price series**" section currently requires
   EPA's "**EMTS transaction data** — transaction-level reported prices" and states that "**The validator must use the
   transaction-level series, not a daily average**". **That requirement is not satisfiable from EPA's published public
   data as published today.** EPA's own data page lists the public price product as "**Weekly volume weighted average
   RIN prices (updated monthly)**" and "**Weekly aggregated RIN transaction volumes (updated monthly)**" (S-439), and
   its price page states that "**The RIN Price chart below shows historical, weekly, volume-weighted average RIN price
   data for separated RINs by transfer date**" (S-440). **Transaction-level EMTS prices are not published.** The
   transaction-level series EPA itself analysed — 2,245,685 usable standard trades over **2013–2021** (S-394) — was
   obtained through the agency's institutional route, and it stops four years before the first moved deadline's
   pre-window. **Accordingly the specification now carries two admissible routes, and the validator must declare
   which one it uses before the holdout is opened:**
   - **Route T (transaction-level).** The validator obtains transaction-level prices through a route outside EPA's
     public data products. It must document the route, the period covered, the vintage and trade-type fields
     available, and the **2013–2021 limit** of the only such series the register has seen.
   - **Route W (weekly VWAP).** The validator runs on EPA's published **weekly volume-weighted average** price series
     by transfer date, D-code and RIN year. Route W is the route the register's **public** evidence supports, and
     three consequences must be pre-registered when it is used: **(i) the estimand changes** from a difference in mean
     *transaction* price to a difference in mean *weekly VWAP*, and the specification must say so in its results and
     must not describe a VWAP result as a transaction-price result; **(ii) the vintage confound becomes
     first-order** rather than a control of second rank, because the published D6 vintage spread on 25 March 2025 was
     **1.375¢/RIN** (S-443) — of the same order as the whole cost floor — and because RINs closer to expiry have
     traded **above** longer-lived RINs "**over dozens of weeks**" (S-404); and **(iii) the announcement contamination
     must be handled as a pre-registered exclusion or adjustment, not left in the treatment window**, because the two
     published announcement effects — D3 **−15 % to $2.70** on the 2024 waiver-and-extension proposal (S-445) and
     **−5 %** on the 2025 delay announcement (S-447, index-rendered) — are of the order of **four to eleven times the
     cost floor** and have the **opposite sign** to the candidate's expectation.
2. **The detectability bound is carried into the kill criteria, and it is stated from published numbers only.** The
   specification's kill criteria are read as amended: a pre-/post-deadline difference on the **public weekly series**
   must be **at least 1.0 – 1.8 ¢/RIN (1.3 – 2.4 % of the published D6 level of 75.375 ¢/RIN)** to be measurable at
   all at n ≈ 9 weekly observations per 60-day window and cell, and must be **at least 0.75 – 1.5 ¢/RIN** to clear a
   minimum round trip (the published same-day traded ranges: D6 75.00–75.75, D4 80.00–81.50, D5 79.75–81.25, D3
   243.00–244.00, **S-443**), with the **stress** multiple from S-404 on top. On the transaction-level series the
   corresponding minimum detectable effect is **≈ 0.02 – 0.09 ¢/RIN** at n ≈ 41,100 per 60-day window. **A specified
   effect below the upper of the two bounds is a *specified null*, and the specification must say so in advance and
   must not report such an outcome as a failed test.** The measurement floor itself is **1.0 ¢/RIN**, because EMTS
   prices are recorded to two decimals (S-441, index-rendered).
3. **The two moved deadlines are confirmed and are usable, and one is now precisely dated.** The 2024 compliance
   year's deadline was extended to "**the first quarterly reporting deadline after the effective date of this action
   revising the 2024 cellulosic biofuel standard**" (90 FR 29751, effective **5 September 2025**) — i.e. **1 December
   2025**; the 2025 compliance year's deadline was extended "**from September 1, 2026, to October 1, 2026**" (91 FR
   56780, effective 4 September 2026) (all three rules at **S-444**). **Both are post-2020, and the trade-type
   decomposition the candidate's forced-flow identification needs — spot, term contract and consignment — is available
   only from 2020** (S-394). The specification's "**The deadline**" section is amended accordingly: the two moved
   deadlines remain **excluded from the primary pooled test**, and each is a **separate, pre-registered event window**
   rather than a poolable observation.
4. **The cost anchor's wording is corrected, and the correction is binding on how the floor may be quoted.** The
   market-quality note must be quoted as the source states it: RINs "**have estimated economic transaction costs that
   *peak* five times higher** than oil, ethanol, and natural gas futures", are "**generally only about one tenth as
   liquid** as comparable commodity futures", and are "**generally five to ten times more volatile**" (S-404,
   line-verified this cycle). **No published cents-per-RIN round-trip magnitude exists** in that document — the cost
   estimates are figure-only — and the specification must therefore quote the **published traded ranges** (S-443) for
   the floor and must **not** convert a modelled multiple into a cents figure.
5. **What has not changed, stated explicitly so that no reader infers a silent change.** The frozen hypothesis, the
   event universe, the windows, the statistic, the controls, the separation rule and the *state-free* scope of this
   specification are **unchanged**; the specification remains a **kill test for the existence claim** and not a trade
   specification; the **conditional** version of IDEA-014 remains retired with its hard stop; **G-20** remains closed
   against the state as specified; and **no specification may be written for the conditional claim**. The
   state-free existence limb's **published-evidence status is unchanged and is now a bounded negative**: no published
   estimate of a pre-/post-31-March RIN price pattern was located (the nearest item, S-442, is a qualitative
   government statement about a **28 February 2013** deadline, with a shared attribution and no published
   post-deadline reversion), so **a null is the expected outcome of this specification**, and the specification must
   report it as such.

### Frozen hypothesis (state-free)

*If the US Renewable Fuel Standard's statutory compliance deadline concentrates price-insensitive demand for
RINs into a fixed annual window, then RIN transaction prices around that window must differ systematically
between the pre-deadline and post-deadline periods — and the difference, if it exists, must be larger than
the friction of trading a RIN. This specification tests only the first half: whether any such difference
exists at all, in a price series the agency itself publishes, and larger than the published friction
anchors.*

### Frozen conceptual rules

- **Event universe.** US Renewable Fuel Standard compliance years **2013–2021** (the window of EPA's own
  EMTS transaction analysis, S-394), and, as an extension, any later year for which the agency has published
  transaction data. **RIN types:** D6 (conventional renewable fuel) and **D4 (biomass-based diesel)**, which
  the agency's own analysis treats separately and which carry materially different prices.
- **The deadline.** The statutory compliance-reporting date is **31 March of the year following the
  compliance year** (S-394: "Compliance dates are generally March 31 of the year following the compliance
  year, unless otherwise extended"), with the moved 2026 deadlines (S-131) and the automatic extensions under
  40 CFR 80.1451(f)(1)(i)(C) recorded separately and **excluded from the primary test** (a moved deadline is
  a different event and must not be pooled with a fixed one).
- **The price series.** EPA's **EMTS transaction data** — transaction-level reported prices for separated
  RINs, by RIN type and vintage, with the agency's own caveats carried forward: the prices are
  **self-reported**, have **limited quality assurance and quality control**, and "in some cases are the
  result of **term contracts** unique to the trading parties" (S-394). The validator must use the
  transaction-level series, not a daily average, because the daily average is what the agency compares
  *against* and therefore cannot be used to measure a departure from it.
- **The windows.** Pre-deadline window: the **60 calendar days ending on the compliance date**. Post-deadline
  window: the **60 calendar days beginning on it**. The window length is **pre-registered** and must not be
  varied after seeing the result; a 30-day and a 90-day variant must be reported as ablations.
- **The statistic.** The primary statistic is the **difference in mean transaction price between the two
  windows**, computed **within RIN type and within vintage**, and **normalised** by the pre-deadline window's
  own mean price so that D6 and D4 are comparable. The **within-year comparison** is the primary design: the
  test is run **for each compliance year separately** and the **sign consistency across years** is the
  primary statistic, with the pooled estimate reported as secondary.
- **The controls (mandatory).** (i) **Vintage contrast** — because obligations may be met with current- or
  prior-year vintages (S-394), the deadline should bite on **current-vintage** demand and not on
  **prior-year** vintages; the **current-vintage minus prior-vintage** window difference is therefore the
  **difference-in-differences estimate**, and it is the primary specification. (ii) **Seasonality** —
  pre-deadline and post-deadline windows straddle the winter fuel season; the validator must control for
  the **same calendar windows in compliance years with no binding RFS obligation**, or use a placebo-deadline
  design (see below). (iii) **Placebo deadlines** — the same window construction applied to **1 August** of
  each compliance year, and to the 31 March of a **synthetic year**, must be reported; a placebo effect of
  the same size as the main effect is a null. (iv) **Exemption-timing confound** — because EPA issued 89 % of
  its small-refinery-exemption decisions after the 90-day statutory deadline (S-393), refineries often did not
  know whether they needed RINs until close to, or after, the compliance date, which may cause "either an
  excess or a shortfall of RINs"; the validator must report the effect **with and without** the volumes
  affected by exemptions, and must state that the exemption timing is a **confound of the deadline itself**
  rather than an alternative explanation of it.
- **The cost floor (both floors must be reported).** Floor 1 (published): the observable dispersion of RIN
  transaction prices around the daily average — **1.1 %** (EPA's central estimate for the 24 small
  refineries), **2.4–2.9 %** (GAO's counterparty-size differential), against EPA's own sensitivity band of
  **5.3 % less to 7.5 % more** (S-393, S-394). Floor 2 (published, weaker): the market-quality cost note
  already on file (S-133). The register states plainly that these dispersion figures are a **counterparty-size
  effect and not a bid-ask spread**, and that **no published RIN round-trip cost estimate was located**
  (**G-38**); the validator must therefore report the result against **both** floors and must not present a
  result between them as tradeable.

### Ambiguities the validator must resolve and record

1. Whether the agency publishes the transaction-level data with enough price granularity and vintage
   labelling to support the within-vintage contrast; if not, the vintage limb is dropped and the test
   reverts to the plain window difference, with the loss of identifying power recorded.
2. Whether "term contracts" dominate the transaction population, and if so, how the validator separates
   spot-like from term transactions without the agency's transaction-type flag; if it cannot, the validator
   must report that the price series mixes horizons and that the window difference is then a statement about
   contract pricing, not about spot prices.
3. Whether the 2013–2021 window contains compliance years with **no** binding obligation (a genuine
   placebo year), and if not, how the seasonality control is built.

### Data fields required

Transaction date; transaction price per RIN; RIN type (D6, D4); RIN vintage year; buyer and seller size
classification (relative market participation over the preceding 182 days, as GAO used); whether the
transaction is separated or attached; the compliance year and its 31 March date; exemption volumes and
decision dates (from EPA's published decisions); and the published RVO and generation data for the
computation of the *net obligated position* — **recorded but not used in the primary test**, because that
state is the retired conditional version's requirement (G-20).

### Timing, execution and survivorship

The test is **state-free and forward-looking in construction only**: every window, deadline, vintage
classification and control must be fixed **before** the prices are examined, and the pre-registration must be
timestamped. Transaction data are reported with a lag; the validator must **not** use a price observation
that was not published by the agency's own reporting date when assigning it to a window, so that the
specification is not silently a backtest on information the market did not have at the time.

### Cost and execution assumptions the validator must justify independently

The cost floor is **published and stated above**; the validator must justify it against S-133 and against the
GAO/EPA dispersion figures, and must state which floor it is testing against. The validator must **not**
assume a bid-ask spread: if it cannot obtain one, the register's published dispersion anchor stands as the
proxy and the result is reported as a **price-discontinuity** result, not a tradeable-return result.

### Pre-specified primary outcome and guardrails

**Primary outcome:** the **within-year, current-vintage minus prior-vintage difference in mean normalised
transaction price between the pre-deadline and post-deadline windows**, and the **sign consistency of that
difference across compliance years**. **Guardrails:** (a) the placebo-deadline estimate must be reported and
must be materially smaller; (b) the D6 and D4 estimates must be reported separately, since the agency's own
analysis shows the price differential is roughly twice as large for D4; (c) the exemption-volume-excluded
estimate must be reported; (d) the result must be reported **against both cost floors**.

### Baselines, separation and controls

The published baselines this test must be read against are the **RIN price formation and pass-through**
literature (S-134, S-135) and the **EU ETS surrender-month premium** (S-101), which is the register's
template for a statutory deadline concession in a credit market and is the reason the US RFS instance is a
separate candidate rather than a re-description of a published result. The **agency-audited price
differential** (S-393, S-394) is a **cross-sectional, counterparty-size** effect and is not a deadline
effect; the two must never be added together or conflated.

### Stress cases, regime slices, ablations

Ablations: 30-day and 90-day windows; D6 only and D4 only; with and without the exemption-affected
counterparties; with and without the vintage difference-in-differences contrast; and the placebo deadline of
1 August. Regime slices: the 2013–2016 RFS2-tightening years against 2017–2021, since the RVO calibration
and the exemption programme both changed over the window (S-201, S-324).

### Pass / fail / uncertain

- **Pass (existence established, direction still unasserted):** a pre-registered window difference that is
  statistically distinguishable from zero, consistent in sign across compliance years, materially larger
  than the placebo-deadline estimate, and larger than **at least one** of the two published cost floors.
  A pass licenses **no** directional claim; it licenses one further step (a specification for the conditional
  claim), which would require re-opening G-20 and locating a signed pre-deadline state.
- **Fail (the candidate's live claim is killed):** no window difference distinguishable from zero, or a
  difference not larger than the published friction anchor, or a placebo effect of the same size. A fail
  **kills the state-free existence limb**; the register's consequence would be to park IDEA-014 (P-015) with
  a terminal score and to record the family in the known-baseline table.
- **Uncertain:** the data cannot support the vintage contrast and the plain window difference is
  indistinguishable from the placebo deadline. An uncertain verdict is **not** a pass and **not** a kill; it
  leaves the candidate unchanged and records what would be needed to decide.

### Kill criteria and follow-up justification

The candidate's last claim is killed by a fail verdict. **The register's own hard-stop conditions apply to
any positive finding:** a positive existence result that is *not* larger than the published friction anchor
is not a result; a positive result that is larger but rests on the exemption-timing confound alone is not a
result either. **Follow-up on a pass:** the only next step permitted by this specification is a written
proposal for a conditional specification, which would require (a) re-opening G-20, (b) a signed pre-deadline
state that satisfies **both** halves of the register's standing requirement — **published before the
deadline** *and* **sign-determining rather than merely informative** — and (c) a fresh G-38 closure on the
RIN round-trip cost. **No state-conditioned specification may be written without all three.**

### Cycle-113 amendment (binding) — the cost floor is restated against the published RIN round-trip cost, because G-38 is now closed and the closure is adverse

Cycle 113 executed the Cycle-112 gap **G-38** — "is there a published estimate of the RIN market's bid-ask
spread or round-trip cost?" — on the two pre-registered route forms, and **closed it** on two published cost
anchors: **S-404** (NERA Economic Consulting, "Ethanol RIN Market Analysis and Potential Reforms", 18 October
2018, filed in EPA docket EPA-HQ-OAR-2018-0775) and **S-405** (Lade, Lin & Smith, "Ex Post Costs and RIN
Prices under the RFS", Resources for the Future Discussion Paper 15-22, June 2015). **This specification is
amended, not re-created.** The frozen hypothesis, the event universe, the windows, the statistic, the
controls, the placebo design and the kill criteria are **unchanged in substance**; the **cost floor** and the
**pass bar** are amended. The section **"Frozen conceptual rules"** (the cost-floor bullet), the section
**"Cost and execution assumptions the validator must justify independently"** and the section **"Pass / fail /
uncertain"** are read as amended by this block; every other section stands as written.

1. **Floor 2 is now a published, market-wide cost estimate, and it is much larger than Floor 1.** On the
   **Roll (1984)** model of the effective spread, the RIN market's frictions are **several times** those of
   comparable energy futures: RIN spreads reach **up to five times** comparable energy markets' spreads,
   transaction costs are of the order of **five times**, market **liquidity is of the order of one-tenth**, and
   RIN **price volatility is five to ten times** that of the comparable energy markets (S-404), with S-405
   supplying an independent academic ex-post cost estimate pointing the same way from an author with no
   commercial interest in the reform. **Both anchors are index-rendered** and the first is a consultancy paper
   prepared for a party with a commercial interest in the reform, so the register relies on the **order of
   magnitude** and not on the point estimates. The body sentence in "Frozen conceptual rules" that records
   "**no published RIN round-trip cost estimate was located** (**G-38**)" is **superseded**: G-38 is closed, and
   the register's own **counterparty-size / not-a-spread** caveat for Floor 1 (the GAO 2.4 %–2.9 % size
   differential, EPA's 1.1 % central premium, and EPA's own −5.3 % to +7.5 % sensitivity band) **stands in
   full** — Floor 1 remains a *dispersion* anchor, not a spread.
2. **The consequence is adverse to the candidate's required effect, and it is material.** A market whose
   round-trip cost is **several times** that of comparable energy futures places a **few-percent** price
   difference **inside** the cost band, not above it. The dispersion anchors the register already holds are
   **small in percentage terms** (2.4 %–2.9 %; 1.1 %; and EPA's own band of −5.3 % to +7.5 %), so a
   pre-/post-deadline price difference of the order the candidate's own premise would suggest is **below** the
   cost floor rather than above it.
3. **The pass bar is therefore amended, and the amendment is a tightening.** The pass condition "larger than
   **at least one** of the two published cost floors" is superseded: because the second floor is now known and
   is **larger** than the first, a pass must clear the **published RIN market cost floor itself** — the
   round-trip cost of the market the test trades in, several times comparable energy markets' costs
   (S-404, S-405). A result that clears the dispersion anchors but not the market-cost floor is a
   **price-discontinuity** result and **not a tradeable-return** result, and must be reported as such. The
   validator must report the result against **both** floors, state which floor it is testing against, and must
   not present a result between them as tradeable.
4. **The kill-criteria follow-up clause is amended because its third condition is now satisfied.** The clause
   "a fresh G-38 closure on the RIN round-trip cost" is **discharged**; the only next step permitted on a pass
   is a written proposal for a conditional specification, which would require (a) re-opening G-20, (b) a signed
   pre-deadline state satisfying **both** halves of the register's standing requirement — **published before the
   deadline** *and* **sign-determining rather than merely informative** — and (c) a **published estimate of a
   pre-/post-31-March RIN price pattern**, which does not yet exist.
5. **What has not changed, stated explicitly so that no reader infers a silent change.** The **state-free
   existence limb remains INCONCLUSIVE** — G-38 asked for the *cost*, not for the *effect*, and no published
   source estimates a deadline-specific price pattern; the candidate's score (**52.0, rank 3**) is
   **unchanged**; **the bar on any state-conditioned specification for IDEA-014 is re-affirmed in full** (the
   conditional version stays retired with its hard stop, G-20 stays closed against the state as specified, and
   no specification may be written for the conditional claim); no `V-` identifier is consumed; and the
   specification remains **executable**.
